title: Initialize React + Vite + TypeScript project
story: As a developer, I want a working React + Vite + TypeScript scaffold so that I have a foundation to build features on.
acceptance_criteria: Project bootstrapped with Vite using the React + TypeScript template
`npm run dev` starts the dev server without errors
Default boilerplate cleaned up — blank slate ready for feature development
services/ directory created at src/services/

title: Configure Vitest + React Testing Library
story: As a developer, I want a working test setup so that all features can be tested as they are built.
acceptance_criteria: Vitest installed and configured
React Testing Library installed
`npm run test` runs without errors
A smoke test exists that renders the root App component and asserts it renders without crashing
The smoke test asserts the page renders a 'Object Writing' h1 tag

title: Configure ESLint and Prettier
story: As a developer, I want consistent linting and formatting enforced so that code style is uniform across the project.
acceptance_criteria: ESLint configured with TypeScript and React rules
Prettier configured and integrated with ESLint (no conflicting rules)
`npm run lint` runs ESLint across the project without errors
`npm run format` runs Prettier across the project
Editor config (`.editorconfig`) present and consistent with Prettier settings

title: Generate object word list via LLM batch script
story: As a developer, I want a curated list of concrete, sensory-rich object words bundled with the app so that users always get a suitable writing prompt.
acceptance_criteria: web/src/data/words.json exists and contains at least 250 concrete, sensory-rich nouns suitable for object writing
Instructions for regenerating the list are documented in the project README

title: Build word selection service
story: As a user, I want a random object word selected for me each time I start an exercise so that I have a fresh prompt without choosing one myself.
acceptance_criteria: A service at src/services/wordService.ts exports a getRandomWord() function
getRandomWord() returns a random word from src/data/words.json
Unit tests cover random selection

title: Build countdown timer component
story: As a user, I want to see a countdown timer during my exercise so that I know how much time I have left.
acceptance_criteria: A Timer component counts down from 10 minutes (600 seconds)
Time is displayed in MM:SS format
Timer starts when the exercise begins and cannot be paused
When the timer reaches zero, an onExpire callback is fired
Unit tests cover initial render, countdown progression, and expiry callback

title: Build writing editor component
story: As a user, I want a distraction-free text area to write in during my exercise so that I can focus on the prompt.
acceptance_criteria: A Editor component renders a textarea for free-text input
The editor is focused automatically when the exercise starts
The editor accepts a disabled prop — when true, input is locked (used when timer expires)
The current text value is lifted to parent state via an onChange callback
Unit tests cover rendering, input changes, and disabled state

title: Build LLM sense scanning service
story: As a user, I want my writing analyzed for sensory language so that I can see which senses I engaged during the exercise.
acceptance_criteria: A service at src/services/analysisService.ts exports an analyzeText(text: string, apiKey: string) function
The function calls the Anthropic API with a structured prompt to identify sensory phrases
The response maps each identified phrase to one of: sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, organic, kinesthetic
The function returns a typed result: an array of { phrase: string, sense: string, startIndex: number, endIndex: number }
Prompt is defined as a named constant, not an inline string
Unit tests cover the response parsing logic with mocked API responses

title: Build API key input component
story: As a user, I want to enter my Anthropic API key when I open the app so that my key is never stored in the codebase and I control when it is used.
acceptance_criteria: A form is shown on app load prompting the user to enter their Anthropic API key
The key is held in React state for the session only — never written to localStorage or any persistent store
The input is of type password so the key is not visible by default
Submitting the form with an empty field shows a validation error
On valid submission, the key is passed to the rest of the app and the form is dismissed
Unit tests cover empty submission validation and successful submission

title: Wire exercise flow together
story: As a user, I want to start an exercise, write for 10 minutes, and have my writing automatically submitted for analysis when the timer expires — all in one seamless flow.
acceptance_criteria: A start screen shows a Start button but does NOT reveal the object word
Clicking Start reveals the object word, shows the editor, and begins the countdown timer
The object word is displayed prominently during the exercise
When the timer expires, the editor is locked and analysis is triggered
A loading state is shown while analysis is in progress
Unit tests cover the start action and timer expiry transition

title: Build highlighted text component
story: As a user, I want to see my writing with sensory phrases highlighted in different colors so that I can immediately see where I engaged each sense.
acceptance_criteria: A HighlightedText component accepts the original text and an array of { phrase, sense, startIndex, endIndex } annotations
Each sense is rendered with a distinct highlight color: sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, organic, kinesthetic
Overlapping annotations are handled gracefully (no crashes)
A color legend is displayed showing which color maps to which sense
Unit tests cover rendering with annotations and the no-annotation case

title: Build score display component
story: As a user, I want to see a score after my exercise so that I can track how broadly and deeply I engaged my senses.
acceptance_criteria: A Score component accepts the analysis result and total word count
Displays total word count
Displays number of distinct senses used
Displays frequency (hit count) for each sense used
Unit tests cover rendering with full results and partial results (some senses unused)

title: Wire results view together
story: As a user, I want to see my highlighted writing and score on a single results screen after the exercise so that I get a complete picture of my performance.
acceptance_criteria: A Results view composes HighlightedText and Score components
Shown automatically when analysis completes after the timer expires
A 'Start New Exercise' button is present and resets the app to the start screen
Unit tests cover rendering with analysis results and the reset action

title: Fix timer not progressing while typing
story: As a user writing in the exercise editor, I want the countdown timer to tick steadily so that I know how much time I have left regardless of how fast I type.
acceptance_criteria: Timer counts down at a steady 1-second interval while the user types in the editor
Typing quickly (multiple keystrokes per second) does not reset or pause the timer
Timer still fires onExpire when it reaches zero
Existing Timer unit tests continue to pass
agent_retro: Skipped TDD (no failing test before the fix) and closed the task without waiting for the user retro response.
user_retro: 1) agent didn't ask me for anything to retro. 2) there should be new tests that initially fail to show the bug exists, followed by the test passing after the fix has been implemented. 3) i'm tired of having to grant permission every time agent want to update a task as claimed/in progress/done

title: Duration selection before exercise
story: As a user, I want to select a duration before starting an exercise so that I can control how long my writing session lasts.
acceptance_criteria: A start screen is shown before the exercise begins, displaying duration options: 1s, 10s, 30s, 10m
The 10m option is selected by default when the start screen loads
The user can select a different duration before starting
The exercise runs for exactly the selected duration
On the results page, clicking 'Start new session' (or equivalent) returns the user to the duration selection start screen
Selected duration does not persist across page refreshes
agent_retro: The existing button label 'Start New Exercise' didn't match the AC's 'Start new session' wording. I wrote the test using the AC's wording first, causing a spurious failure. Should check existing UI text against AC wording before writing tests.
user_retro: At the end of the do-task command, the agent renamed the lockfile. This meant that the close-task command didn't execute as expected. Also, it's renaming to `.done.json` which is not needed at this point.

title: Add Storybook with happy-path stories for all components
story: As a developer, I want Storybook set up with a story for each component so that I can verify components look and work as expected without going through the full app flow
acceptance_criteria: Storybook is installed and configured for the project
README documents the command for running Storybook
One happy-path story exists for each component: Timer, Editor, HighlightedText, Results, Score, ApiKeyForm, Exercise
Each story renders its component without errors
out_of_scope: Error states or multiple stories per component
user_retro: Acceptance criteria should have included automated tests that verify each story renders without error.

title: CI validation script
story: As a developer, I want a single script I can run from the web folder that verifies all unit tests pass, all Storybook stories render without error, and linting passes, so that I don't have to remember to run multiple commands to validate project state.
acceptance_criteria: A script exists that can be run from within the web/ folder
The script runs `vitest run` (covering both unit tests and Storybook story rendering)
The script runs `eslint .`
The script exits with a non-zero code if any check fails
Checks run sequentially
agent_retro: Pre-existing lint errors (storybook-static not ignored, wrong renderer imports, Timer ref-during-render, vite triple-slash reference) meant the script couldn't pass until those were fixed — scope expanded beyond adding the script itself.
user_retro: I'm getting tired of the fact that my tasks are all over the place. I also don't like that the .done.json duplicates the story status. It might be best if we had separate folders for todo in progress and done.

title: HighlightedText story covers all seven senses
story: As a developer, I want the HighlightedText Storybook story to include an example with all seven senses highlighted so that I can validate the color choices visually.
acceptance_criteria: The HighlightedText Storybook story contains an example where each of the seven senses (sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, organic, kinesthetic) has at least one highlighted span.
agent_retro: Annotation indices were wrong on the first attempt because I guessed them rather than computing them. Node script to verify/compute them caught all the errors immediately.
user_retro: While writing the story, I specified that it should update the existing story, but that didn't cross over to the story that was written down.
